extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in commutative algebra / algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and formal statements about Hilbert series/polynomials, Hilbert–Samuel functions, filtrations, graded/Rees algebras, primary decomposition in graded settings, and the dimension theory (Krull dimension, height, regular local rings, completion) in Noetherian/graded contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert–Serre form of Hilbert series (Thm 20.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under: R = ⊕ R_n a graded ring with R0 Artinian, R finitely generated R0-algebra, and M a finitely generated graded R-module. Then H(M; t) can be written H(M; t) = e(t) t^l / Π_{i=1}^r (1 - t^{k_i}) with e(t) ∈ Z[t], l ≥ 0, and integers k1,...,kr ≥ 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by writing R = R0[x1,...,xr] with xi in degree ki and induction on r; use exact sequences induced by multiplication by xi, additivity of length, and finite-generation properties. The statement gives an explicit rational form for the Hilbert series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness and Hilbert polynomial when degrees are 1 (Cor 20.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R = R0[x1,...,xr] with xi ∈ R1, and M ≠ 0, then H(M;t) = e(t) t^l /(1-t)^d for unique e(t) ∈ Z[t] with e(0) ≠ 0, e(1) ≠ 0, some integer l, and d = r - deg(e). There is a polynomial h(M;n) ∈ Q[n] of degree d-1 with leading coefficient e(1)/(d-1)! such that ℓ(M_n) = h(M;n) for n ≫ 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take all ki = 1 in the Hilbert–Serre form; uniqueness follows from unique factorization. The asymptotic equality ℓ(M_n)=h(M;n) holds beyond an explicit threshold (n ≥ deg(e)+l).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration, q-filtration, and stable filtration (Def 20.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A filtration of M is a descending chain M = M0 ⊇ M1 ⊇ M2 ⊇ ... . It is a q-filtration if q M_n ⊆ M_{n+1} for all n, and stable if q M_n = M_{n+1} for n ≫ 0 (equivalently q^n M_m = M_{n+m} for n ≥ 0 for some m). The q-adic filtration Mn = q^n M is stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stable filtrations are the ones that eventually behave like powers of q; stability is crucial for finiteness and polynomiality results (Hilbert–Samuel theory).

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated graded ring/module construction (Def 20.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a q-filtration, the associated graded ring G_q(R)=⊕_{n≥0} q^n/q^{n+1} and G_q(M)=⊕_{n≥0} M_n/M_{n+1} are defined, with multiplication induced by representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: G(R) and G(M) encode the 'leading term' information of the filtration and are graded objects whose Hilbert series relate to Hilbert–Samuel series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert–Samuel function/series/polynomial (Def 20.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all quotients M/M_n have finite length, then n ↦ ℓ(M/M_n) is the Hilbert–Samuel function; its generating function P(M; t) = Σ ℓ(M/M_n) t^n is the Hilbert–Samuel series. If ℓ(M/M_n) is eventually a polynomial in n, that polynomial is the Hilbert–Samuel polynomial pq(M; n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the filtration is the q-adic one, write P_q(M; t) and p_q(M; n). Existence of pq and its degree/leading term are central invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of G(R) and G(M) for stable filtrations (Lemma 20.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R is Noetherian, q an ideal, and M finitely generated with a stable q-filtration, then G(R) is generated as an R/q-algebra by finitely many elements of q/q^2, and G(M) is a finitely generated G(R)-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses generation of q by finitely many elements and that stable filtration gives a finite generating range for graded pieces of G(M). This underpins rationality/polynomiality results for Hilbert series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Samuel's theorem linking P(M;t) and H(G(M);t) (Thm 20.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be Noetherian, q an ideal, M finitely generated with a stable q-filtration, and assume ℓ(M/qM) < ∞. Then for every n, ℓ(M_n/M_{n+1}) < ∞ and ℓ(M/M_n) < ∞, and P(M; t) = H(G(M); t) · t/(1 - t).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to the quotient by Ann(M) and apply Lemma 20.12 to deduce finite generation and then compare generating series. This expresses the Hilbert–Samuel series in terms of the Hilbert series of the associated graded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and uniqueness of Hilbert–Samuel series and polynomial (Cor 20.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Samuel hypotheses and with q generated by r elements and M ≠ 0, P(M; t) has unique form e(t) t^l /(1 - t)^{d+1} with e(0) ≠ 0, e(1) ≠ 0, l ∈ Z and r ≥ d ≥ 0; there is a polynomial p(M; n) ∈ Q[n] of degree d with leading coefficient e(1)/d! and ℓ(M/M_n) = p(M;n) for n ≫ 0. The polynomial pq(M; n) differs from p(M;n) by degree ≤ d-1 and the degree and leading coefficient are independent of the stable q-filtration chosen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This pins down the pole order at t=1 (hence degree) and leading coefficient invariance; use earlier theorems and the relation between P and H(G(M);t).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rees algebra and equivalence with stability (20.16–20.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rees algebra R(q) = ⊕_{n≥0} q^n is a graded ring. For a module M with a q-filtration, R(M) = ⊕_{n≥0} M_n is a module over R(q). R(M) is finitely generated over R(q) if and only if the filtration is stable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finite-generation of R(M) over R(q) is both necessary and sufficient for stability; this gives an algebraic criterion to check stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin–Rees lemma for stable filtrations (Lemma 20.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Noetherian, M finitely generated, N ⊆ M, q ideal, and M = M0 ⊇ M1 ⊇ ... a stable q-filtration. Define N_n := N ∩ M_n. Then N = N0 ⊇ N1 ⊇ ... is a stable q-filtration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof via finite generation of the Rees algebra/module; the lemma is the key technical tool ensuring intersections of submodules with filtered pieces are stable filtrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact-sequence behavior for Hilbert–Samuel polynomials (Prop 20.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0 of finitely generated modules and q ideal, M/qM has finite length iff M'/qM' and M''/qM'' do. Then pq(M) = pq(M') + pq(M''), degree pq(M) ≤ max(deg pq(M'), deg pq(M'')), and deg pq(M) = max(deg pq(M'), deg pq(M'')).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use supports and Artin–Rees to pass to stable filtrations and additivity of lengths; cancellation of leading terms explains the degree formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneous components, submodules and homogeneous maps (20.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a graded module M = ⊕ M_n, the homogeneous components are M_n; a submodule N is homogeneous if it is the direct sum of its intersections with each M_n. A map φ: M' → M is homogeneous of degree r if φ(M'_n) ⊆ M_{n+r}. Kernels and cokernels of homogeneous maps inherit natural gradings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This fixes the notion of homogeneity used in graded primary decomposition and graded domain considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion for a homogeneous submodule to be p-primary (Prop 20.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R Noetherian graded, M finitely generated graded module, Q homogeneous submodule. If whenever homogeneous x∈R and homogeneous m∈M satisfy xm ∈ Q but m ∉ Q then x ∈ p := nil(M/Q), then p is prime and Q is p-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives a test for when a homogeneous submodule is primary by checking initial homogeneous components and the nilpotent annihilator; proof uses decomposition into homogeneous components and minimality arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneousness of annihilator and nilpotent elements (Exercise 20.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: For graded R and graded M, the ideal a, Ann(M), and nil(M) are homogeneous ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses grading compatibility and decomposition into homogeneous parts; useful when analyzing associated primes in graded situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation by homogeneous elements preserves primaryness (Exercise 20.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Q is a primary submodule of a graded module M and Q^{(3)} denotes the submodule generated by homogeneous elements of Q, then Q^{(3)} is primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus primary components can be replaced by homogeneous-generated primary components when passing to graded decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homogeneous primary decomposition exists (Thm 20.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian graded ring R and finitely generated graded module M, any homogeneous submodule N has all associated primes homogeneous and admits an irredundant primary decomposition in which all primary submodules are homogeneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain by taking any primary decomposition and replacing each primary component by the submodule generated by its homogeneous elements; irredundancy preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graded domains and homogeneous elements in fraction field (20.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R = ⊕ R_n is a graded domain with fraction field K, an element z∈K is homogeneous of degree n if z = x / y with x ∈ R_m and y ∈ R_{m-n}. The subsets K_n form a graded subring whose degree-0 part is a field and whose nonzero degree indices form a subgroup of Z; hence after renumbering K is K_0(x) for a transcendental x in degree 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the structure of the fraction field of a graded domain and how to renumber degrees to get a polynomial-like structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integral closure preserves grading (Thm 20.29)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let R be a Noetherian graded domain with fraction field K, and let R̄ be its integral closure in K. Then R̄ is a graded subring of K; integral closure respects the grading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses integral dependence, finite-module arguments, and homogeneity to show that homogeneous components are integral and hence lie in R̄; relevant for comparing Hilbert polynomials of R and R̄.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of dimension of a module (21.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a module M, dim(M) := sup { r | there is a chain of primes p0 ⊊ p1 ⊊ ... ⊊ p_r in Supp(M) }. For Noetherian R and finitely generated M, dim(M) = max dim(R/p0) where p0 runs over minimal primes in Supp(M).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dimension is the Krull dimension of the support; it ties prime chains to geometric/topological dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter ideal and system of parameters (21.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For M nonzero, rad(M) is intersection of maximal ideals in Supp(M). An ideal q ⊆ rad(M) is a parameter ideal of M if M/qM is Artinian. For Noetherian semilocal M, q is a parameter ideal iff q′ = Ann(M)+q contains a power of rad(M). A system of parameters (sop) is a minimal set x1,...,xs in rad(M) with ℓ(M/⟨x1,...,xs⟩M) < ∞; s(M) denotes the minimal such s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter ideals generate finite-colength quotients and are used to define d(M) (degree of Hilbert–Samuel polynomial) and s(M) (minimal number of parameters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation dim(M) = d(M) = s(M) for semilocal modules (Thm 21.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Noetherian ring R and nonzero finitely generated semilocal module M one has dim(M) = d(M) = s(M), where d(M) is the common degree of Hilbert–Samuel polynomials for parameter ideals and s(M) the minimal number of elements generating a parameter ideal (size of a system of parameters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by induction using Lemma 21.3, behavior of Hilbert–Samuel polynomials under exact sequences, and prime-avoidance to lower dimension by quotienting by a well-chosen element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Behavior of dimension under quotient by element (Lemma 21.3 & Cor 21.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: For x ∈ rad(M), (1) s(M) ≤ s(M/xM) + 1. (2) dim(M/xM) ≤ dim(M) - 1 if x ∉ p for any p ∈ Supp(M) with dim(R/p) = dim(M). (3) deg pq(K; n) ≤ deg pq(M/xM; n) ≤ d(M) - 1 where K = Ker(M →^{x} M). Corollary: dim(M/xM) ∈ {dim(M), dim(M)-1} with equality criterions involving zero-divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact sequences and Artin–Rees type arguments; choose x avoiding top-dimensional primes to strictly lower dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Height of a prime and relation to minimal ideals (21.6 & Cor 21.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Height ht(p) = sup{ r | chain of primes of length r ending at p } equals dim(R_p). Corollary: ht(p) ≤ r iff p is minimal over an ideal generated by r elements; equivalently p minimal containing some r-generated ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a generator-count criterion for height; converse is shown by localizing and lifting generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krull Principal Ideal Theorem (Thm 21.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If R Noetherian, x ∈ R, and p is prime minimal over ⟨x⟩, then if x is not a zero-divisor (x ∉ z.div(R)) we have ht(p) = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows height-one primes arise from principal elements that are non-zero-divisors; proof reduces to contradiction with associated primes if height were 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local ring definition and characterization (21.18 & Prop 21.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Noetherian local ring A of dimension r is regular if its maximal ideal m can be generated by r elements; equivalently dim_k(m/m^2) = r. Equivalently, A is regular iff its associated graded ring G_m(A) is a polynomial ring in r variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The associated-graded characterization uses degrees of Hilbert series and counts of generators of graded pieces; conversely, surjectivity/injectivity arguments show G_m(A) ≅ polynomial ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular local rings are domains (Thm 21.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: A regular local ring A is an integral domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Induction on dimension: quotienting by a parameter yields a regular local ring of smaller dimension which is a domain, so the parameter is prime; use prior exercises to conclude domain property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generation of ideals in regular local rings and regular s.o.p. (Prop 21.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is regular local of dimension r and a ⊆ A is an ideal with B = A/a regular of dimension r-s, then a is generated by s elements and any such s elements extend to a regular system of parameters of A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact sequences on graded pieces m/m^2 and counting dimensions to deduce minimal number of generators and extendability to a regular s.o.p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtration topology, a-adic topology and completion conventions (22.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a filtration M = M0 ⊇ M1 ⊇ ..., define a topology with basic open sets m + M_n. For an ideal a, the a-adic filtration and topology are standard; any two stable a-filtrations give the same a-adic topology. Mn are closed; the closure of a submodule N is ⋂_{n≥0} (N + M_n). M is separated (Hausdorff) iff ⋂ M_n = {0}; M is discrete iff {0} is open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity of addition and scalar multiplication is automatic for a-adic filtrations; stability ensures topological invariance. These topological properties are the starting point for constructing completions and inverse-limit formulations.
